original_value: The blockchain is the underlying technology of the Bitcoin cryptocurrency, and it has created much excitement in the technology and research communities. A blockchain is a distributed ledger collectively maintained by a peer‐to‐peer network of participants who in Bitcoin are known as miners. This key innovation enables cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin to operate in a decentralized manner with no intermediaries such as financial institutions. But the blockchain can be used to record things other than cryptocurrency transactions. While many of the concepts of Bitcoin build on what have been around since the 1980s and 1990s, the designer(s) of it have made important assumptions that make it work along with the use of an incentive protocol, leading to a major breakthrough from traditional academic thinking. In this paper, we present the state‐of‐the‐art of blockchain and cryptocurrencies along with research challenges and opportunities that would be of interest to researchers getting into this exciting field.

result.paraphrase: Blockchain, the foundational technology behind Bitcoin, has generated considerable interest in both technology and research circles. It is a distributed ledger jointly maintained by a peer-to-peer network of participants, called miners in Bitcoin. This important innovation allows cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin to function in a decentralized way without intermediaries such as financial institutions. Beyond cryptocurrency transactions, blockchain can also be used to record other kinds of data. Although many Bitcoin concepts draw on ideas dating back to the 1980s and 1990s, its designer(s) introduced crucial assumptions and an incentive protocol that made it work, marking a significant departure from traditional academic thinking. In this paper, we survey the current state of blockchain and cryptocurrencies, along with research challenges and opportunities for researchers entering this exciting field.
